=================== README.md
# Discourse Graphs Review Lab

> **Alpha. LLM-created. Not yet tested in real team use.** This project attempts
> to accurately represent the current workflow used to review Discourse
> Graphs PRs. That workflow is constantly in flux. This package is an evolving
> draft, not an established team process or a guarantee of review correctness.

Automated synthetic checks have been run. They are recorded separately in
[Testing](docs/testing.md) and do not establish teammate, macOS or live-provider
acceptance. The alpha status applies even when automated checks pass.

This private repository packages DG PR triage, pinned detailed reviews, changed-head
refreshes and offline HTML. It keeps one shared assessment record and renderer.
Local review progress is separate from GitHub approval. Provider collection is
read-only and limited to the configured repository in the DiscourseGraphs organization.
The example target is `DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph`; DG Roam and Obsidian clients
remain legitimate review surfaces.

## Start with synthetic data

Use Python 3.11+ (`python3` on macOS). No provider access is needed:

```sh
python scripts/team_review.py sample
```

Open `local/synthetic/index.html`. The example is synthetic DG-shaped data, not a
real PR snapshot. Read [TEAM-INSTALL.md](TEAM-INSTALL.md) for configuration,
authentication, operation, updates and cleanup. The repository source is
`https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/review-lab`.

To preview concrete before/after explanations without provider access:

```sh
python skills/mg-review-lab/scripts/review_lab.py render --input examples/narratives.json --output local/narratives/index.html
```

Open `local/narratives/index.html`, choose either synthetic PR and expand
“The change, explained.” These examples show a published field moving and a
reader's field preference changing, with pseudocode and local diff jumps.

## Use with Codex

Read [mg-review-lab](skills/mg-review-lab/SKILL.md) and supply an explicit local
configuration. The skill routes queue refresh, targeted review, saved prioritization
and HTML rendering. A complete refresh includes fresh evidence and assessment of
every changed/new snapshot. Collection or re-rendering alone is not a code review.

Keep real PR records, source evidence, notes, credentials and local configuration in
ignored `local/` or a private output directory. Do not commit them. Cloning does not
install global skills, profile commands, schedulers or services. No review submission,
comment posting, automated fixes, merging or deployments are included.

## Included

- Configurable reviewer, DG repository, evidence paths and stable localhost port.
- Detached inspection, immutable diff pins and source evidence retained after cleanup.
- Intent/scope assessment, findings/checks, Guided walkthroughs and optional Shape maps.
- Shared offline renderer, local notes/progress and matching-snapshot state transfer.
- Concrete change examples and before/after pseudocode, with legacy narrative support.
- DG-only collector guards and synthetic regression tests.

See [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [portability](docs/portability.md),
[provenance](docs/provenance.md) and [roadmap](ROADMAP.md).
Bundled third-party licenses are retained. No blanket license is granted here.
=================== TEAM-INSTALL.md
# DG alpha installation and operation

Alpha, LLM-created, not yet tested in real team use. This evolving package attempts
to reflect the current DG review workflow, which is constantly in flux.
Canonical DG source: https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/review-lab (private).
Automated synthetic checks are documented separately in docs/testing.md.

## Required tools and access

| Operation | Requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Synthetic rendering, saved HTML, local server | Python 3.11+, browser; standard library only |
| Requested-PR discovery and pinned preparation | Git, authenticated GitHub CLI (`gh`), repository read access |
| Intent assessment | Linear read connector or supplied dated issue/comments/spec evidence |
| DG review prose | Configured target checkout's `.agents/skills/dg-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` |
| Optional Shape maps | Node.js 18+, pinned TypeScript 5.5.4; follow `docs/shape.md` |
| Product verification | Target repository instructions and its toolchain; package tests do not replace them |

Credentials stay in GitHub CLI / connector stores. Do not put tokens, raw provider
evidence or local paths in committed configuration. A teammate needs access to the
private canonical repository; granting access or moving ownership requires a team
decision. No account permissions were changed by this draft.

## Install a reviewed source revision

```sh
git clone https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/review-lab.git review-lab
cd review-lab
```

Select the reviewed commit before use. Keep local configuration/data outside tracked
source and export matching notes/progress before updates.

From the cloned source directory, use the following commands. On Windows run `python`; on macOS
run `python3` for every command below. No `npm install` is needed for core rendering.

```sh
python scripts/team_review.py sample
python -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'
```

Open `local/synthetic/index.html`. The same shared renderer emits the auxiliary
Archives and Notes pages. This proves rendering without a personal profile function.
It does not exercise provider access or perform a code review.

Copy `team-review.example.json` to `local/team-review.json`. Change all relative
paths so they resolve from that config file's directory. Alternatively use absolute
paths, using forward slashes in JSON on both systems. Set `repository` to a verified DiscourseGraphs repository, `repo_root` to its checkout, and `reviewer` to `authenticated` or a
verified GitHub login. Set disjoint `output_dir` and `temp_root` outside the reviewed
checkout. Set `writing_skill` to the actual DG writing skill. Choose one stable
local server port and browser profile for persistent notes.

```sh
python scripts/team_review.py --config local/team-review.json doctor
gh auth login
python scripts/team_review.py --config local/team-review.json doctor --auth
```

`doctor` is offline by default. `--auth` makes harmless identity/repository reads;
it never logs in or grants scopes. If authentication or connector approval stalls,
report the gap and continue with supplied evidence. No retry loop is defined.

## Codex discovery

For the pilot, tell Codex: “Read `<package>/skills/mg-review-lab/SKILL.md` and
`<package>/skills/mg-review-lab/references/team-setup.md`; use my configuration at
`<config>`.” This needs no global skill installation or personal workflow manager.
All package procedures and supporting skills stay in the canonical repository.

After approval, the maintainer can add a forwarding entry in the team's chosen
discovery collection. It must resolve `REVIEW_LAB_REPO` or an explicit checkout
path, verify the canonical remote and load this repository's skill. Do not install
copied renderer/assets or overwrite an
existing `mg-review-lab` discovery entry. Collision resolution belongs to the owner.

## Queue, review and refresh

1. Collect requested PR metadata with `queue`. This is collection only. It uses
   configured reviewer identity and canonical direct-request / re-request eligibility,
   paginates reviews and timelines, and records exclusions and observation time.
   Search reaching 1,000 results fails with an explicit coverage gap.
2. Ask Codex to triage the eligible PRs from `evidence/queue.json` using the canonical
   queue procedure. Intent, readiness and next action need source evidence. A metadata
   collection is not an assessment or a complete refresh.
3. Prepare selected PRs with `prepare`. The canonical helper creates an isolated
   clone and detached worktrees, verifies GitHub head pins, computes merge bases,
   and discovers competing Linear references. Read its complete manifest.
4. Retrieve full linked intent/comments with pagination. Save dated captures and
   provenance under the run's `context/` or durable evidence directory. Inspect the
   pinned diff and callers; author findings, criteria assessments and exact checks.
   Keep unavailable sources, unrun checks and failed checks visible.
5. Author one shared `lab.json` following `references/record-contract.md`. Use the
   canonical import adapters where useful (`review_lab.py import-review` or
   `import-queue`), then assess the resulting record. Do not pass standalone queue
   schema data directly to the shared renderer. Follow the packaged
   [narrative guide](skills/mg-review-lab/references/narrative.md) for concrete change
   explanations. Newly authored narratives use format version 2; choose a small
   example and before/after rule when they clarify the change. Reauthor older
   narratives from their matching source during a requested review or refresh.
6. Recheck head, base and direct request identity before delivering the current
   review. Changed pins invalidate old findings, passed checks and local completion.
   Refresh requires reassessment of every changed/new snapshot, not just re-rendering.
7. Render and serve the shared record. Export supported notes/progress before
   upgrading or changing origin. Import only state whose snapshot identities match.
8. Run `cleanup` for each prepared manifest in success or failure paths after
   preserving authored records/check logs. It retains pinned diffs, metadata and
   context outside the temporary clone. Dirty inspection worktrees are preserved
   for inspection. Cleanup does not remove durable evidence or rendered HTML.

```sh
python scripts/team_review.py --config local/team-review.json queue
python scripts/team_review.py --config local/team-review.json prepare --pr 123 --linear-ticket 123=ENG-456
python scripts/team_review.py --config local/team-review.json render --input /path/to/lab.json
python scripts/team_review.py --config local/team-review.json serve
python scripts/team_review.py --config local/team-review.json cleanup --manifest /path/to/prepare-manifest.json
```

These commands are documented for future authorized operation. Recorded checks are synthetic/local validation, not real team acceptance. `serve` uses the existing hidden loopback server and
opens no browser. It rejects conflicting servers instead of changing the origin.
Local completion and notes never approve GitHub or change Linear. No provider-write
command, automated fix, comment-resolution loop or scheduler is added.

## Updates and removal

Export local state. Preserve the config, `lab.json`, evidence, archives and browser
origin. Check the canonical checkout is clean; fetch and inspect the proposed next
release commit, then switch explicitly and rerun offline smoke/tests and doctor.
Do not merge unrelated local source changes automatically. Re-render saved data;
this does not fetch providers. Verify overlapping state imports preserve matching
snapshots and invalidate changed heads. File Viewed/theme are outside the supported
state export and remain browser-local, as documented upstream.

Removal: stop only the server started for this package, remove only the owned
forwarding discovery entry if one was installed, and preserve/export private review
data. This draft does not add install, auto-start, update or removal automation.

## Acceptance still required

Record OS/version, Python/Git/gh versions, selected source commit and exact commands
for each pilot. Windows synthetic validation is recorded in the task evidence.
macOS commands are documented but **not validated** on this host.

- Team owner confirms canonical repository access and release/discovery source.
- One Windows teammate and one macOS teammate bootstrap without another contributor's filesystem.
- Each discovers their own requests, triages one PR, opens one pinned detailed review,
  and re-reviews a changed head with visible invalidation.
- Exercise notes/progress export/import, missing Linear, failed check, provider
  authentication failure, clean cleanup and dirty-worktree preservation.
- Confirm no GitHub/Linear state changed; scope/escalation and QA proposals remain
  proposals until their own human review. No automated audits or rollout.
=================== AGENTS.md
# Discourse Graphs Review Lab

This alpha, LLM-created repository owns its packaged skills, scripts, references,
schemas and renderer. Read README.md, TEAM-INSTALL.md, docs/architecture.md and
skills/mg-review-lab/SKILL.md before changing implementation.

Keep collection limited to the configured DiscourseGraphs repository. The default
example target is DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph. Apply the target DG repository's
instructions and its dg-engineering-writing-style source. DG's Roam and Obsidian
clients are in scope. Generic libraries/tools needed by the DG workflow remain valid.

Use synthetic fixtures for tests. Keep real provider records, source evidence,
credentials, local configuration, browser state and personal notes out of commits.
Use ignored local/ or a private output directory. Retain bundled third-party licenses.

Use one shared renderer and record contract across review modes. Edit source assets
and regenerate output. Do not replace a requested assessment with metadata collection.
Keep pins, freshness checks, visible verification gaps and local progress independent
of GitHub approval. Clean managed inspection worktrees while preserving evidence.

No provider writes, fixes, deployments, scheduler changes or global skill installation
are implied by a review request. Do not refresh providers merely to validate source
or documentation. Report untested team/macOS behavior and source reconciliation gaps.

# Windows and macOS setup

=================== docs/architecture.md
# DG review architecture

| Location | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| scripts/team_review.py | Configured DG entry point and durable evidence preservation |
| scripts/dg_scope.py | Shared DiscourseGraphs collection boundary |
| skills/mg-review-lab | Public skill, shared record, offline renderer and collectors |
| skills/mg-pr-review-html | Pinned standalone review preparation and rubric |
| skills/mg-pr-review-queue-html | Isolated pinned queue preparation and validation |

An agent derives intent from sourced DG criteria, inspects immutable code and records
assessment/check evidence. Python embeds assets and data into offline HTML. The renderer
does not infer correctness. Shape uses optional Node/TypeScript against pinned Git objects.

The [narrative authoring contract](../skills/mg-review-lab/references/narrative.md)
defines concrete examples, before/after pseudocode and their validated diff targets.
Narrative format version 2 renders those blocks directly and separates code steps
from verification/source disclosures. Legacy narratives retain their flow layout.
Presentation upgrades do not refresh assessments, checks or local review progress.

Read TEAM-INSTALL.md for the local config. Queue/audit/discussion collectors enforce
DG ownership; queue searches use one configured repository. The target checkout is
read-only during preparation. Inspection clones/worktrees and output remain separate.
Cleanup preserves patches, metadata and source context before removing a clean run.

The localhost server serves saved output; starting it does not fetch providers.
Keep one browser origin/profile to retain state. Supported export/import covers notes,
Guided progress, priorities, saved views, local PR completion and desk notes/tasks.
File Viewed and theme preferences remain separate browser-local state.

The repository under DiscourseGraphs owns this alpha package. Any future discovery
entry must load its actual skill source without copying the renderer. Local profile
functions and hosted/site synchronization are outside this repository's setup.
=================== skills/mg-review-lab/SKILL.md
---
name: mg-review-lab
description: Operate the Discourse Graphs Review Lab dashboard. Use for refreshing the review index or queue, reviewing or rechecking a PR in Review Lab, reprioritizing saved reviews, opening the dashboard, or changing its UI. A refresh includes complete assessments of new or changed PRs.
---

# Review Lab

For portable team setup, first read
[team setup](references/team-setup.md) and use the explicit local configuration.
Use configured local paths and verified reviewer
identity while retaining the existing shared renderer and review contracts.

One entry point for the dashboard and its review workflows. Infer the mode from the
request; the user does not need to invoke separate triage and review skills.

## Choose the requested operation

| Request | Procedure |
| --- | --- |
| Refresh Review Lab, the index, or the queue | Follow the [complete refresh contract](references/queue-refresh.md). Resolve current membership, collect fresh pinned evidence, assess every new or changed PR, update effort/risk/explanations/Guided/Shape, preserve archives and matching state, and validate/render the index. |
| Review or recheck a specific PR | Follow the [individual review procedure](references/review-workflow.md) for that PR. Preserve unrelated queue entries and assessments; a targeted PR need not currently request the configured reviewer's review. |
| Reprioritize or choose what to review next | Use [queue evidence and prioritization](references/queue-workflow.md) and [triage policy](references/triage-policy.md), with saved assessments and explicit observation dates. Do not imply a fresh code review. |
| Change the dashboard | Read the [current UI contract](references/current-ui.md), relevant presentation references, and the [record contract](references/record-contract.md) if data changes. Edit source assets/scripts and validate the affected behavior. |
| Open or start the dashboard | Follow [local operation](references/local-operation.md) and [local setup](references/current-experiment.md). `review-lab` / `reviewlab` opens saved data; it does not refresh providers. |

A refresh is the complete process by default. Do not stop after fetching PRs or ask
the user to invoke a second skill for assessment. Honor an explicit narrower request
(for example, comments only or collection only) and identify the partial result.
If a request combines modes, complete each relevant part without repeating shared work.

## Shared implementation

For authored change explanations, follow the [narrative guide](references/narrative.md):
name the changed object or flow, show a concrete before/after example when useful,
and explain the decision with pseudocode when it helps. New narratives use format
version 2; old saved narratives stay readable.

All lab scripts, assets and references live beside this skill. Use the packaged
`mg-pr-review-html` and `mg-pr-review-queue-html` helpers when a procedure calls for
them; they also retain separate standalone uses. The record and offline renderer are
shared across modes, with one assessment per pinned PR snapshot.

Keep review data and evidence in the configured private output directory or ignored
`local/`. Retain the established browser origin and matching notes/progress. A request
to refresh or assess PRs does not authorize posting provider reviews/comments or merging.
=================== skills/mg-review-lab/references/local-operation.md
# Local review operation

These scripts use a durable demo directory containing index.html, lab.json and evidence/. Use the configured output directory from TEAM-INSTALL.md. Never replace a current review with a triage-only refresh when the user requested actual reviews.

## Start the existing UI

Run `python <skill>/scripts/serve_review_lab.py --directory <demo>` and open the printed HTTP URL in Codex. It reuses a matching server or starts a hidden static Python server at 127.0.0.1:8769. A conflicting server is left alone. Keep the origin stable: file:/// and other ports have different browser storage. This does not launch Codex tasks, refresh PRs, or install an auto-start service.

## Extra diff context

After pinning and inspecting Git revisions, run `python <skill>/scripts/collect_diff_context.py --input <lab.json> --output <lab.json> --repo <inspection-checkout>`, then use the normal renderer. This reads Git objects without checkout changes. Each hunk gets at most ten matching unchanged lines on each side, bounded by adjacent hunks. Missing/binary/non-UTF8 objects omit expansion. The renderer keeps this context out of changed-line totals and default layer context exports. Recollect after revisions change; do not reuse old arrays on new heads.

## Separate PR checklist audit

The unified skill includes `scripts/collect_audit_queue.py`, `scripts/build_pr_checklist.py` and `assets/pr-checklist-template.html`. Both scripts take `--directory <demo>`. The collector accepts `--repository DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph` and `--reviewer authenticated`; search and prior queue membership are limited to that repository. Collection is GitHub read-only and needs authenticated gh. It checks direct pending requests and re-request timelines, including PRs from the existing queue. Respect API pagination/truncation limits; do not claim completeness if collection is incomplete.

The builder consumes lab.json, evidence/audit-queue.json, evidence/current/queue.json and evidence/body-audit.json. Retrieve each PR body and assess Loom URLs, other video URLs, scope-check statements and local-review statements before rendering. Preserve exact supporting text and collection timestamps; checked claims are not independent verification. name: mg-pr-review-html
description: Review a GitHub pull request against its diff and Linear intent, then generate a visual HTML review connecting scope and specs to implementation, evidence, findings, and an ordered walkthrough. Use for PR reviews, HTML reviews, review one-pagers, or review-plus-explanation requests.
---

# PR Review HTML

Create a read-only, evidence-based PR review. Never change GitHub state, the PR branch, or the active worktree. Never launch a nested `codex` process.

## Workflow

1. Use `dg-engineering-writing-style` from the owning Discourse Graph repository for all review prose. For the portable team pilot, resolve and verify its explicit `writing_skill` configuration through [team setup](../mg-review-lab/references/team-setup.md). If the skill is unavailable, report the missing dependency; do not substitute a personal writing style.
2. Confirm the PR belongs to the current DiscourseGraphs repository. Non-DG targets are rejected.
3. Prepare a detached worktree from the repository root. Checkouts live under `<repository>/local/reviews/.worktrees/<run>/worktree`; manifests, JSON, and retrieved context live under `local/reviews/.runs/<run>/`. Both are locally ignored:

```powershell
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" prepare --pr 123
```

Add `--linear-ticket ENG-1855` when the request names a ticket. Omit `--pr` only when the current branch has a PR. Preparation otherwise searches the PR description, then the first three PR comments for a Linear reference. Inspect other relevant links in PR metadata and retrieved context.

4. Read the printed manifest, generated instructions, and schema completely.
5. If a Linear candidate was discovered, retrieve the full issue and every comment with the connected Linear read tools. Follow comment pagination. Read directly relevant linked tickets, scope/spec docs, and design decisions. Save retrieved material in `run_dir/context/`; put source metadata and requirement assessments in the review JSON. Record inaccessible or conflicting sources. Never update Linear or external documents.
6. Review only the manifest's pinned base-to-head diff in its detached worktree. Inspect surrounding code and run proportionate checks.
7. Write one JSON object at `review_json` that exactly matches the schema.
8. Finalize the review:

```powershell
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" finalize --manifest <manifest-path>
```

Finalization always removes the temporary worktree unless preparation used
`--keep-worktree`. If the review JSON is invalid, it preserves the small run artifacts
for correction but still removes the worktree. A later `prepare` also reaps abandoned,
non-retained worktrees from runs older than 12 hours.

9. Report every generated HTML path. Open a page only when asked.

## Worktree maintenance

Run these from the repository root using the same `generate_pr_review.py` script:

```powershell
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" list
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" cleanup --stale --dry-run
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" cleanup --stale
```

Use `cleanup --all` for all non-retained runs, or `--pr 123` to narrow a batch. `--dry-run` prints paths without removal. Batch cleanup skips `--keep-worktree` runs; clean a retained run explicitly with `--manifest <path>`. Run artifacts are preserved by default. Add `--remove-artifacts` to remove that run's JSON/context too; rendered HTML remains.

Older version 2 manifests still support cleanup of their exact system-temp checkouts. Cleanup does not scan/delete arbitrary temp folders. Failed Git removal and unregistered directories containing files are preserved for inspection, with an actionable path. Use the Git-aware cleanup command rather than deleting a registered worktree in Explorer.

## Review contract

- Apply `references/codex-review-rubric.md` as the authoritative finding rubric. Only its output shape is replaced by `assets/review-output-schema.json` (version 2).
- Report actionable problems introduced by the PR. Keep findings diff-anchored, with evidence and a practical correction. Requirements reference finding IDs instead of repeating the bug.
- Organize the page around behavioral change, intent and evidence, reviewer attention, and one ordered walkthrough. Omit empty sections. Do not generate separate changed-area summaries, review maps, or beginner lessons.
- Prefer visual explanations when they reduce reading: multiple complementary visuals are welcome. Choose graph/architecture, state, sequence, decision table, before/after pseudocode, or actual UI screenshots. Follow [visual guidance](references/visual-explanations.md). Do not force a diagram for a trivial change or repeat the same explanation in several formats.
- Derive requirements from retrieved tickets/specs, not the implementation. Distinguish implementation assessment from verification. Cite sources and pinned code; link exact checks by ID. Show source conflicts and unexpected scope as explicit reviewer decisions.
- Keep review findings and verification status separate. Failed checks, unrun checks, unverified requirements, and missing intent context remain visible near the header even when no blocking bug was found.
- Use one sentence for the change summary. Short prose and concrete examples are preferred; no bullet quotas. Keep walkthrough items focused on one behavior with a reason to inspect it.
- Background and quizzes are opt-in for an explicit learning request. `learning` and `quiz` are optional and collapsed; no fixed question count.
- Wrap identifiers, paths, fields, and commands in backticks. Use light inline formatting where useful.
- Keep raw ticket descriptions/comments in local context artifacts, outside the HTML. Link PR, source documents, branches, and pinned commits. Preserve run artifacts on success while removing the temporary worktree.
- Keep generated artifacts local. Do not post comments, submit reviews, apply fixes, alter branches, add labels, or modify tracked ignore files.

## Failure handling

- Stop if `git` or `gh` is unavailable or unauthenticated.
- Linear failures do not block the code review. Record the exact failure in `linear_context`.
- If finalization rejects the JSON, fix only the invalid structured output and retry.
- If any step after preparation cannot complete, clean the worktree before returning while
  preserving diagnostic artifacts:

```powershell
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" cleanup --manifest <manifest-path> --keep-artifacts
```

## Resources

- `references/review-prompt.md`: PR-specific review and writing requirements.
- `references/codex-review-rubric.md`: finding threshold and review behavior.
- `assets/review-output-schema.json`: structured review contract.
- `scripts/generate_pr_review.py`: prepare, finalize, and cleanup workflow.
- `scripts/render_review.py`: self-contained HTML renderer.


## Primer presentation

Use GitHub Primer styling for review HTML, with bundled semantic light/dark tokens and native HTML controls. Follow [Primer design guidance](../mg-review-lab/references/primer-design.md). Preserve offline exports and existing review interactions.

When producing the shared review lab, include an authored Pseudocode tab for every queued PR. Follow [the lab pseudocode contract](../mg-review-lab/references/pseudocode.md), inspecting the pinned code and retaining failure paths and review caveats. Generate through the canonical lab renderer rather than patching HTML.

name: mg-pr-review-queue-html
description: Triage a queue of related GitHub pull requests, review selected PRs against Linear intent at a risk-proportionate depth, and produce a polished offline HTML dashboard with compact evidence-backed review capsules. Use for PR review queues, ordered multi-PR review, rereviews, or individual PR reviews where reducing context switching matters.
---

# PR Review Queue HTML

Review GitHub pull requests without changing GitHub, Linear, the source checkout, or its active worktree. Produce local, self-contained HTML as the primary deliverable. Never post comments, submit reviews, change labels or branches, update Linear, apply fixes, or launch a nested model process.

## Choose the mode

- `triage`: mandatory first pass for a queue. Gather only enough evidence to assess intent, ticket linkage, change surface, risk, readiness, dependencies, semantic center, and next action.
- `standard`: normal selected-PR review. Validate the behavioral contract, intended scope, semantic center, tests, and actionable introduced findings.
- `deep`: standard review plus wider call-site tracing, richer explanation, diagrams, selected excerpts, and additional proportionate checks. Use only for high-risk or explicitly requested depth.
- `rereview`: compare the last reviewed immutable head SHA with the current head and revisit unresolved findings. Do not rebuild unchanged explanation.

Read [references/modes.md](references/modes.md) for the selected mode. Read [references/data-contract.md](references/data-contract.md) before writing or validating structured review data. For a performance/cache evaluation, also read [references/evaluation.md](references/evaluation.md). Apply [references/codex-review-rubric.md](references/codex-review-rubric.md) whenever deciding whether an issue qualifies as a finding.

## Two-pass workflow

1. Resolve the local repository without modifying it. Use a temporary clone/worktree for code inspection. Pin every PR to its GitHub-reported head SHA and compute the merge base against the fetched base in that isolated clone.
2. In pass 1, triage every requested PR. Record draft/CI state, unresolved decisions, missing intent, ticket-link status, diff size and areas, likely semantic center, risks, dependencies, and a recommended next action. Do not perform deep explanation or exhaustive checks.
3. Perform the mandatory scope check for each PR:
   - Prefer a Linear ticket explicitly supplied by the user for that PR.
   - Always discover references from GitHub metadata, even with an explicit selection. Retain contradictory candidates and their sources as ambiguity evidence while keeping the explicit ticket selected; make missing or multiple candidates prominent.
   - Retrieve the issue, comments, blockers/blocked-by links, parent/sub-issues, and relevant project or milestone context with read-only Linear tools. Preserve provenance. Failure to retrieve Linear never aborts code review.
   - Derive intended outcomes, acceptance criteria, and explicit non-goals. Compare them with the immutable base-to-head diff, separating implemented scope, missing scope, and out-of-scope additions.
   - Promote an actionable scope gap to a normal diff-anchored finding only when it satisfies the review rubric. Keep ambiguity and non-actionable gaps out of findings.
4. Order the queue only when evidence supports it. Explicit Linear relations outrank stacked-base and explicit GitHub references; those outrank structural or semantic inference. Label inferred relations low-confidence, preserve provenance, expose conflicts/cycles, and never manufacture a total order.
5. Select pass-2 mode and PRs from triage. Match effort to risk and readiness. If draft state, failing CI, missing intent, or an unresolved upstream decision makes detailed review premature, say so and recommend the next action.
6. Find the small semantic center of each selected diff and recommend the few files or areas requiring human attention. Run proportionate checks in the isolated worktree and record exact commands and outcomes.
7. Write one review-package JSON object following `assets/review-package.schema.json`, validate it, then render the queue dashboard. The first screen of each PR capsule must cover intent, behavioral contract, implementation path, scope alignment, primary risks, reading order, checks, readiness, and verdict. Put neutral comprehension before critical assessment.
8. Keep generated artifacts under a user-selected local output directory or a temporary directory. Do not edit tracked ignore files. Report all generated paths.

## Deterministic helper

Use `scripts/pr_review_queue.py` for repeatable logic:

Now I'm thinking through how to run proportionate checks in a pinned worktree that lacks node_modules — possibly symlinking it from the main checkout to avoid a fresh install.

I'm deciding that a frozen pnpm install inside the worktree is acceptable since the shared pnpm store makes it fast via hardlinks, as long as nothing is installed in the main project directory and unrun checks are recorded honestly. Postinstall scripts running from our own repo should be safe in this context.

I should also remind them to avoid bare npx and instead use pnpm exec or the local node_modules binaries. And I need to lay out firm boundaries: no writes to GitHub or Linear, no touching my own checkout or the review-lab tracked sources, no running cleanup since it covers both PRs together, no git stash since refs are shared, and no modifying the other PR's directory or rendering the final combined page themselves — though a self-check render of their own single-PR page is fine.

Their final report back to me should be short — under 300 words — covering verdict, findings with severity and location, suggested fixes, requirement gaps, which checks ran and passed or failed, and anything unrun or blocking, without dumping raw HTML.

I also want them to pass me facts rather than conclusions, since this is meant to be an independent review and I don't want my own opinion baked in. I decide it's fine to mention since it's a fact relevant to scope — the reviewer should judge the PR against whatever criteria the third part claims to cover, reading the PR body to understand the split. They'll also pull additional context like the reviewer brief through the raw GitHub metadata in the manifest. For the import-queue adapter, the review package needs certain fields, but I'll let the agent work that out on its own. On freshness, I'll have them mark it current if the head still matches at delivery time. Brief sizes look fine, so I'll launch both tasks in one message as background jobs and then narrate the results.

Write only under `/mnt/data/projects/review-lab/local/review-data/runs/2026-11-03/pr-1576/`: `package.json`, `lab.json`, `index.html`, `context/`, `checks/`.

- No GitHub or Linear writes: no comments, reviews, labels or status changes.
- No fixes to the PR, and no commits or pushes anywhere.
- Do not touch `/mnt/data/projects/discourse-graph` (the user's checkout) except to read the writing skill.

- Checks run, each with pass or fail, plus checks you could not run and why.
- The `lab.json` path, and confirmation that `validate` passed.
- Anything that blocked you or that you had to work around.
